races.name: Tom McCormack Memorial Cup Maiden Hurdle
Massey Ferguson Johnston Farm Equipment Longford Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: King Of The Greys
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for Peter Fahey who habitually fades late — recent form reads 4-0-8-8-P and sim-going record shows zero wins or places on Good; needs something to go very wrong for the prominently placed horses to pick up a piece of this.

runners_data.name: Malbas
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, expected to bowl along uncontested from flag to flag; the ⚠ fade flag is the key concern, as the 10-year-old has finished in the back half of fields repeatedly on similar Good ground, and an amateur in the saddle adds a layer of doubt about pace judgement.

runners_data.name: Whispering Willow
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old has solid form on Good going — won at 16f on Good, placed twice over 19-20f on Good — and travels prominently, making this the most naturally suited profile to the expected race shape; LR 18 days is a comfortable prep.

runners_data.name: Friar Hogan
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin partners this hold-up horse who has shown one placed effort in seven similar-going starts; the tongue-tie is new headgear worth noting, and the five-year-old will need a messy race or a strong gallop to get competitive from the rear.

runners_data.name: I'm Flattered
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose best form has come at shorter trips (11f, 16f) and who has failed to land in the money over similar distances on Good; the tp headgear combination is familiar but offers little encouragement over 2m3f.

runners_data.name: Burlington House
runners_data.note: Showed genuine ability when second over 16f on Heavy for Oliver McKiernan but is operating off a 67-day break, and as a true hold-up type, will find himself racing in mid-division here purely because the field is stacked with rear-hangers — his natural closing game will be compromised.

runners_data.name: Circus Act
runners_data.note: The p headgear flags a horse who has been ridden for a finishing run in the past; Keith Donoghue takes the ride on a seven-year-old with one win on Good at 14f, and the step up to 2m3f on this track is untested territory in the form book.

runners_data.name: Flash The Badge
runners_data.note: Zero wins or places from five runs in similar going for John McConnell's five-year-old; the 72-day layoff is significant, and the habitual fade flag makes this a very difficult winner to construct from any scenario.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Legitimate prominent runner with two wins in her profile, though both were recorded at shorter trips and on softer ground — the combination of stepping up in trip and meeting a quicker surface has caught her out before; Peter Smithers (7lb claimer) is a negative on this competitive handicap mark.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is the clear positive on this Gordon Elliott-trained six-year-old, but the horse's natural style is to be held up and his p headgear reinforces that — forced into mid-division here by sheer numbers, the 10-day turnaround suggests Elliott finds him well, yet the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Demanding Gerry
runners_data.note: A consistent placer on Good ground — four seconds and a fourth in his last five starts — for James Andrew Fahey; races prominently and clearly handles this trip and surface combination, making him one of the most natural fits to the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Movie King
runners_data.note: 316 days off the track for V C Ward is an enormous flag; the nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who has placed over 20f on Good but will face a massive fitness ask on return after almost a year away.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: Third over 20f on Good just 12 days ago for I Madden, showing live fitness; Paddy Cleary (7lb claimer) keeps the ride but this horse's true style is to be held up and, though recent form is the best of the rear-rankers, it will still need the race to be run to suit closers.

runners_data.name: Dark Berkshire
runners_data.note: Consistent fade in form — 8-9-7-P-0 in recent starts — and zero wins or places from eight runs on similar going; held up by style and mapped to mid-division, this six-year-old has very little in the data to commend it.

runners_data.name: Finnicky Filly
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's eight-year-old races prominently and has placed five times on Good going, though a win has eluded her in seven similar-going efforts; the t headgear is familiar and she will be competitive in the early stages, but the 0-from-32 trainer stat over 14 days is context.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good and has multiple places on similar ground, so the conditions are fine — off just 17 days and in good order; a natural hold-up horse who will find mid-division is the best he can achieve positionally, which blunts the closing run he needs.

runners_data.name: Il Pirata
runners_data.note: Reserve runner for Mrs Lorna Fowler whose style is unknown — the B entry code flags a breathing issue and 0 wins from five runs on Good ground; if he runs, the unknown style is a risk in a 19-runner field at a tight track.

runners_data.name: Mambo Du Large
runners_data.note: Four-year-old reserve for M K Flannery who is lightly raced and has only three hurdle runs on record; if he takes his place he will be exposed as inexperienced in this deep field and the hold-up style over 2m3f looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 17f on Good for Denis Hogan — genuine recent form — but is a hold-up horse by profile and will be squeezed into mid-division again; the b headgear is familiar and the ⚠ fade flag is a concern given the tactical compromise he faces.

races.paceDynamic: Malbas is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals capable of disputing the lead in a race this size, he is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good ground over 2m3f. Behind him, Whispering Willow, Barrogstown Girl, Demanding Gerry and Finnicky Filly are the legitimate prominent types who will fill the chasing positions, creating an orderly, strung-out shape rather than a chaotic scramble for position. The field does hold significantly more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Burlington House, Sneddy Eddie, Movie King, Dream Shaper and Surviving Murmansk are all true hold-up horses who will be pushed into mid-division simply by weight of numbers, meaning they will not get the clean, late run their profiles demand. With a single front-runner setting an uncontested, measured gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently from the start who can travel within themselves, attack the last and sustain the effort on a fair surface — prominent-style runners who don't need a fast pace to be found travelling well are the primary beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Malbas Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Malbas sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominently placed chasers — Whispering Willow, Demanding Gerry, Barrogstown Girl — travel smoothly behind him throughout.
scenarios.body: Malbas dictates a fair but not punishing tempo, and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and sustained galloping from the turn in; horses who have been racing prominently all the way have the initiative over the closers who have ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Stayer Reels In
scenarios.trigger: If Malbas goes too steady in the early stages and fades predictably in the closing stages, allowing a strong-travelling prominent horse to take it up and quicken.
scenarios.body: Whispering Willow, who has already won on Good and shown form over similar trips, is ideally placed to inherit the lead and make it a true test of stamina through the final hurdles; Demanding Gerry, who has repeatedly placed in this shape, is equally suited to pressing on from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and several prominent types fade, opening a gap for horses held up in mid-division to come with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Dream Shaper ran third over this trip recently and Surviving Murmansk has the fitness edge off just 17 days, giving them the best credentials among the repositioned types; however, most horses in this group are not natural closers and are here only because numbers forced them back, which limits the likelihood of a clean late finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At Big Field Kilbeggan
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant interference, a loose horse or jumping errors that fragment the field and disrupt the settled order.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners at a tight track, a spill or loose horse could nullify any tactical advantage and create a lottery where sole survivors rather than the best horses dominate; King Of The Greys or Friar Hogan, both patient hold-up types comfortable tracking trouble, could benefit if chaos culls the prominent brigade.

watchPoints.text: Malbas sets the entire tempo — if he goes too steady or fades abruptly from 2 out, the race collapses and the prominent chasers inherit it without warning; watch his jumping and gallop rhythm from the start as this dictates whether Scenario A or B plays out.

With 19 runners at Kilbeggan's tight track, the first two hurdles are a serious crowding risk — watch for any interference that shuffles Whispering Willow or Demanding Gerry back from their prominent positions, as losing those berths in a field this large is very hard to recover.

Sneddy Eddie (Jack Kennedy) is a horse with prominent trainer form and a top jockey who may attempt to secure a better position than his natural hold-up style suggests — if Kennedy pushes to the front third early, that changes the pace equation for Malbas.

Backinabit won last time and carries live form, but the hold-up style and fade flag mean the eye will catch him staying on without quite getting there — do not confuse a late run with a genuine winning move; his positional compromise is real.

Movie King returns after 316 days off the track — monitor in the parade ring for condition and watch for any signs of a blow-up or jumping errors early that could cause interference for the tightly packed midfield runners.

races.name: Massey Ferguson Johnston Farm Equipment Longford Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: High Notions
runners_data.note: OR 99 hold-up performer who has placed twice in similar good-ground conditions; Michael Kenneally (5) takes off valuable weight, but 40 days off and a pattern of finishing in the 7-10 region on recent starts tempers confidence in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Fabhcun
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old with a headgear flag (p) has struggled to reproduce early promise, returning two blanks in five runs with no wins or places on good ground; 55 days off and a hold-up style make this a tough ask at 165lbs.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: Returning after just 14 days with blinkers fitted (t), this seven-year-old has won and placed heavily on good ground over 18f trips — the strongest similar-going record in the field — and has the physical profile to travel prominently even if naturally a hold-up type.

runners_data.name: O'Grady Cracker
runners_data.note: A 101-day absence is a significant flag, and the fading-in-finish warning combined with a poor recent form string (9800-) on variable ground suggests J J Slevin faces a stiff task off OR 94 on a retrieval mission.

runners_data.name: Dearg Mor
runners_data.note: Tongue tie and a held-up style for Aidan Anthony Howard's five-year-old; two consecutive fourth-place finishes on good ground over 24f suggest the trip is not an issue, but 157lbs and a crowded hold-up division reduce the chance of securing a useful position.

runners_data.name: Rare Times
runners_data.note: Style listed as unknown, making tactical projection difficult; Danny Mullins takes the ride which is always worth noting, but three runs only, all in held-up fashion in the 5-7 finishing zone, and 77 days off leaves plenty of uncertainty around this four-year-old.

runners_data.name: Rizedda
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse carrying a fade warning and a redistribution tag — meaning in a field this size she is unlikely to find her natural position at the rear; Darragh O'Keeffe rides and the horse's good-ground record (5 of 6 runs) is a mild positive, but racing outside her comfort zone blunts her chance.

runners_data.name: Brianna Lily
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old with two places from 15 good-ground starts, Brianna Lily operates naturally at the back of the field; shunted into midfield on the map because of the crowded hold-up division, her best form comes from further back than she is likely to find today, 8 days since last run is sharp.

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Brian Hayes aboard, with 17 days since last run; Lariat has placed twice in 15 good-ground outings and at OR 83 and age 10 will be uncontested in front, giving her every chance to dictate a modest gallop that could carry her much further than market expectations suggest.

runners_data.name: Patrick Street
runners_data.note: Winning form at OR 82 on good ground and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 highlights how far from his natural role this horse is likely to operate today; Daniel King's mount has placed three times from a hold-up position, but in a crowded rear division he will struggle to reproduce that from midfield.

runners_data.name: Laligurash
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with only three hurdle runs (all on good ground), Alan O'Sullivan (5) in the saddle, fade flag and redistribution tag all noted; the limited form base (8-7-12) and a natural hold-up style that won't be fulfilled in this field make meaningful selection very difficult.

runners_data.name: Little Boy Sivola
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's five-year-old has been in the 5-14 finishing range across nine good-ground starts and carries both a fade warning and redistribution note; Tiernan Power Roche takes the ride but the horse has yet to win or place under this mark despite regular opportunities.

runners_data.name: Tawny Lea
runners_data.note: Only three runs visible in the form (08R), one a refusal, and the fade warning is significant; Alex Harvey takes the ride for Thomas Coyle but 45 days off, limited exposed form and a hold-up style that won't find natural expression in this race all count against the six-year-old.

runners_data.name: Thirsty Work
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with a heavy-going bias (6 of 7 runs on soft or heavy) and a 0-from-11 record on good or good-to-soft; Phillip Enright rides but the going switch looks damaging and the blinkers (t) have not yet unlocked anything meaningful.

runners_data.name: Western Opera
runners_data.note: STYLE_FIT of 0.92 with a genuine tendency to hold up; however, Western Opera has shown ability to place on good ground over 22f trips and the Conor Stone-Walsh booking for Kieran Callaghan carries minor stable form interest with a better recent run (4th, 22f, good).

runners_data.name: Bangor Lady
runners_data.note: Joshua Halford (7) aboard for John Patrick Ryan, who has been firing plenty of runners (6/32 in 14 days); the six-year-old's form is poor (7F-008) on good ground, the fade flag applies, and the redistribution away from the rear means a natural asset is compromised.

runners_data.name: Brohatna
runners_data.note: No jockey listed is worth flagging as a market watch; M M Rice's six-year-old has placed four times in five good-ground runs and operates best from a hold-up or mid-division berth, making her one of the more likely beneficiaries if she can track close enough to the pace in a steadily-run contest.

runners_data.name: Lakewood Rose
runners_data.note: OR 98 and the highest-rated genuine prominent runner in the race, giving her the key positional advantage behind Lariat; consistent placed form (four top-four finishes in last five on good ground) and the ability to travel on the pace makes her the most obvious danger on race-shape grounds.

runners_data.name: Light Her Up
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago — the sharpest turnaround in the field — and her hold-up style will find no natural expression in this crowded rear division; Hugh Paul Finegan's eight-year-old has placed once in nine good-ground outings and the quick reappearance adds a clear physical question.

races.paceDynamic: Lariat is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse field and should lead from the outset at Kilbeggan, setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop that suits a horse whose recent form shows stamina over pace. With no rival likely to challenge for the lead, Lariat can control tempo from the front, keeping fractions honest rather than gruelling — a scenario that rewards prominent racers who can track close to the pace rather than deep hold-up types who need a strong gallop to reel in. Lakewood Rose is the one legitimate prominent racer able to press Lariat and sit in the ideal position throughout, while Brohatna and Bowgate Street have the form profile to travel comfortably in the first half of the field. The race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can race close to the pace — prominent and early-tracking profiles — because the absence of pace pressure means closers will find the early tempo too steady to generate the late sectionals they depend on. This field contains far more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Rizedda, Laligurash, Brianna Lily, Little Boy Sivola, Tawny Lea, Thirsty Work, Western Opera, Bangor Lady and Light Her Up are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, with Lakewood Rose and Brohatna the horses best-placed to actually secure a tracking berth near the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lariat Controls; Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lariat sets a steady, uncontested lead and Lakewood Rose or Brohatna track close enough to strike turning for home.
scenarios.body: Lariat's unchallenged lead keeps the pace honest, meaning the horses who travel prominently or in a close-tracking position conserve energy and arrive at the final hurdle with something to give; stamina and position are the twin advantages here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On; Front Runs Home
scenarios.trigger: If Lariat's controlled gallop is so uncontested that the leader simply keeps finding all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: A 10-year-old with a history of front-running and good-ground form, Lariat can steal a winning margin if rivals spend too long travelling and leave the challenge too late over this 2m3f trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong-Travelling Midfielders Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally more searching than expected and horses from a mid-division berth arrive with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Bowgate Street has a strong record on good ground over similar distances and has won from a holding position before; Brohatna's consistent placed record at this level suggests she can pick up from mid-division if the race develops with a touch more tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens materially in the back straight, stringing out the field and creating genuine end-to-end gallop that allows hold-up types to finish through.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given a lone front-runner in Lariat who has no reason to go fast; the many redistributed hold-up horses — Rizedda, Brianna Lily, Patrick Street — are racing out of their natural role and would need an unusually strong pace to generate meaningful late momentum.

watchPoints.text: Lariat (Brian Hayes) will lead from flag-fall with zero competition for the role — watch whether Hayes exploits the uncontested lead to steal a significant advantage rounding the final turn.

Lakewood Rose is the only prominent runner with the OR (98) to press or track Lariat at a comfortable pace; if she jumps well and slots into second early, she is in the optimal position for the race shape.

The sheer volume of redistributed hold-up horses — nine runners including Rizedda, Brianna Lily and Patrick Street — means the midfield will be unusually congested; watch for interference, horses being denied a clear run and traffic problems at hurdles in the back straight.

Bowgate Street returns after only 14 days with blinkers fitted (t); the headgear change and quick turnaround are worth monitoring in the betting — if support comes, Philip Donovan's position in running will be the key indicator of whether the stable is bullish.

Light Her Up ran just three days ago — the quickest reappearance in this field — and any significant market move for a horse with no jockey confirmed should be treated with curiosity rather than confidence given the physical demands of a back-to-back run.

races.name: Tote Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: In The Trenches
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with excellent Good-ground form (sim-going 13/15, 1W7P) and wins at this trip range; Keith Donoghue aboard for Cromwell, 24-day break should have him fresh, and sitting just off Magic Day is his natural comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Magic Day
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will set the pace from flag to finish; De Bromhead yard in fair form (T14: 6/41) and Good ground suits (9/11), but the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag reflects that today's field may push him harder than ideal — he is the engine of the race shape, not necessarily the winner.

runners_data.name: Laxxio
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Anthony Mullins, Danny Mullins in the saddle; limited Good-ground wins (0W1P in 3/6 similar runs) but placed here suggests he handles the surface, though a step up from 17f to 19f could test stamina reserves.

runners_data.name: Andys Flame
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse fitted with tongue-tie and pads, nine-year-old veteran; won over this exact 20f trip on Good last season (sim-going 1W4P) but the 7lb claimer Shane Fitzsimons is a notable stable-form risk (T14: 0/27) — needs the pace to genuinely collapse.

runners_data.name: In For The Night
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose form string shows worrying tail (7,8,16,11,19) in recent starts, yet with two previous wins on Good over similar trips; 49-day break and O'Dwyer (T14: 1/2) is a micro-stable — hard to trust on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Silly Mongoose
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with headgear (hood/tongue-tie); won over 16f on Good recently and stepped up to 20f adequately, Good-ground profile reasonable (1W1P in 6/7), but needs something to go wrong up front to get competitive.

runners_data.name: You Done Well
runners_data.note: Naturally a prominent racer — consistent placed form (5,2,3,3,4 in five runs) who handles Good well (1W4P in 8/15 similar) — pushed into a midfield role here by the congested pace map, which dims the chance this represents compared to a smaller-field race where he could press.

runners_data.name: Mon Sheriffe
runners_data.note: Has recorded only completions of 6th or worse in six similar-going runs with no wins, so even setting aside that his front-running instincts are frustrated by this deep prominent field, his raw ability on the evidence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Tudorista
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a tidy recent fourth over 20f on Good (sim-going 6/6 all Good), but form figures of 4,12,9,8,4 over similar trips suggest a consistent placed ceiling rather than a winning profile; Phillip Enright gives a competent pilot.

runners_data.name: Marlpark
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago — very short recovery time — and has a form string of 0,0,4,P,F including a fall; a genuine hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield only adds to the complications; blinkers fitted but current form and freshness are genuine concerns.

races.paceDynamic: Magic Day is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected, will be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable clip from the outset, controlling tempo around Kilbeggan's tight 2m3f circuit. In The Trenches, Laxxio, and In For The Night will push to track Magic Day prominently, but the field contains a surplus of prominent-minded horses — You Done Well, Mon Sheriffe, and Marlpark are all natural pressing types who cannot all claim their preferred position and will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts. With Magic Day uncontested and the pace likely to be honest rather than scorching on Good ground, the race shape most favours horses who can settle just off the leader and produce a sustained effort from two out — true prominent-to-handy types with proven Good-ground form — rather than genuine closers who must make up ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Magic Day Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Day is allowed to dictate from the front without serious challenge and sets a measured, sustainable gallop.
scenarios.body: Magic Day pings from the front, keeps the field strung out at a controlled pace, and the prominent chasers in close attendance are the main dangers as stamina kicks in from the third-last; hold-up horses off a slow tempo will struggle to generate enough momentum to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If In The Trenches or Laxxio travel powerfully just off Magic Day and surge past at the second-last before the field bunches.
scenarios.body: A strong pace from Magic Day combined with a prominent stalker delivering a smooth challenge turns this into a two-horse final-furlong duel; horses who settle and travel with purpose in the first half of the race benefit most here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected, burning out the front-runners and opening the race to hold-up horses charging late.
scenarios.body: Andys Flame or Silly Mongoose, both genuine hold-up types with proven Good-ground form, rattle home if the leaders use each other up over the final mile; this scenario requires a genuinely hot early tempo which the pace map does not strongly support.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and the field concertinas, turning the finish into a scramble for runners squeezed out of position.
scenarios.body: Redistributed prominent types like You Done Well and Mon Sheriffe, forced wide and without their natural rhythm, must produce career-best efforts to grab a piece; this shape is least likely given Magic Day's clear front-running role and the dependable Good ground.

watchPoints.text: Magic Day's uncontested lead could become a decisive advantage — watch how quickly Darragh O'Keeffe establishes him and whether any rival moves to challenge before the halfway point.
Marlpark ran only three days ago and lines up having fallen last time out; Daniel King will need to place him carefully to avoid interference risks in a 10-runner field at a tight track.

You Done Well and Mon Sheriffe are both natural front-running types compressed into midfield — watch for covering moves or crowding at the first few hurdles as riders try to recover their preferred positions.

In The Trenches has the strongest combination of Good-ground evidence and prominent style to suit this pace shape — watch whether Keith Donoghue sits close enough to Magic Day to make a move from the third-last.

Andys Flame is the most interesting hold-up runner on going credentials but watch whether the pace is strong enough to bring him into it — if Magic Day coasts, closer types may simply run out of ground.

races.name: Hurley Family Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Barton Sky
runners_data.note: Lightly raced eight-year-old with an unknown preferred style (U), 425 days off the track — the lengthy absence is a significant concern over a marathon trip, and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim only partially compensates for the ring rustiness.|

runners_data.name: Clone Cross
runners_data.note: Recent form includes two fallers and a pull-up but has placed twice on Good ground over 2m, most likely to feature if grabbing a prominent spot; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim helps, though the five-year-old's reliability is questionable after that form string.|

runners_data.name: Installment
runners_data.note: True hold-up type partnered by Danny Mullins, 55 days off; his four runs on Good ground produced zero wins or places, which is a concern, though the step up to 3m½f could play to a staying pedigree if he travels into the race.|

runners_data.name: Le Questionnaire
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old is the one confirmed front-runner and Jack Kennedy takes over in the plate; three of his last four runs on Good or similar produced two seconds, but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests he is racing out of his more typical role here, and his stamina over 3m½f at this pace must be respected rather than assumed.|

runners_data.name: Lord Lackendarra
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse with headgear (p), 22 days since last run and placed three times from 15 starts on comparable going; the trip looks right for him but his tendency to race from the rear means he needs things to fall perfectly in a race with limited pace.|

runners_data.name: O'Callaghan Can
runners_data.note: Style unknown for this five-year-old, placed twice on Good ground, and the step up to 3m½f with Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim could prove significant if he settles into a prominent position; 10 days since last run suggests fitness is fine.|

runners_data.name: Ruled By The Sun
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse (hg:t) with only two runs to his name — both finishing seventh — and just one comparable Good-ground run; while the headgear change is noted, the thin form profile makes him very difficult to assess over this demanding trip.|

runners_data.name: Rusty Harkness
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe rides this De Bromhead six-year-old who has placed twice on Good ground at a mile-and-a-half to three miles; style unknown but recent second on Good over 22f suggests he handles the conditions, and 64 days off means fitness needs proving.|

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's six-year-old has placed twice on Good going and carries headgear (tp), but she is a genuine hold-up horse whose true style means she faces a difficult task securing her natural position in a rear-heavy field; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she is mapped to midfield rather than where she would want to race.|

races.paceDynamic: Le Questionnaire is the one confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner maiden over 3m½f on Good ground at Kilbeggan, and with Jack Kennedy in the plate for Gordon Elliott, he is likely to stride to the front and attempt to control tempo from the outset. The pace he sets should be sustainable rather than frenetic — he faces no genuine challenger for the lead — meaning he can bowl along at a measured gallop and conserve energy through the early stages of this marathon trip. Giorgia Rose is a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear of the field is crowded with hold-up horses; she is unlikely to replicate her natural style here and her chance must be tempered accordingly. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting an honest but manageable pace over a stamina-sapping trip — strongly favours horses with proven hold-up/prominent finishing ability who can track the pace comfortably and deploy a sustained late run, particularly those with demonstrated stamina at this sort of trip on Good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Le Questionnaire Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Le Questionnaire is allowed to roll at his own rhythm unchallenged and the pace remains honest enough to stretch the field without burning him out.
scenarios.body: Le Questionnaire controls every yard, the field strings out behind him on this demanding trip, and any runner without stamina is exposed in the final mile; horses who travel prominently without expending energy chasing will find themselves best placed in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stamina Stayers Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and Le Questionnaire weakens before the last, allowing hold-up horses with proven stamina to overhaul him.
scenarios.body: The strong pace over 3m½f on a tight track saps Le Questionnaire's reserves and the race becomes a stamina test in the final half-mile, suiting horses who have been produced with a run to spare.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking horse travels fluently just off Le Questionnaire and produces a more decisive turn of foot than the leader in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: With Le Questionnaire potentially flattening out having led for so long, a horse who has tracked in second or third and jumps the last hurdle with momentum can run him down; this suits a horse that travels confidently in close proximity to the pace on a switchback course.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late, bunching the field, and hold-up horses produce a late flourish from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the true hold-up types are squeezed by the field dynamic and redistributed; Giorgia Rose would be the prime beneficiary if she can somehow get cover and produce her run, but her style fit in this shape is compromised.

watchPoints.text: Le Questionnaire's stamina is the pivotal question — watch whether Jack Kennedy allows him to coast at a true gallop or if he is forced to quicken at any stage, as the moment the pace lifts he becomes vulnerable to stayers behind him.

Giorgia Rose carries a STYLE_FIT flag and is mapped out of her natural hold-up role — watch whether Donagh Meyler actively pushes her forward or drops her in, as a mismatch between her style and race shape could cost her any realistic chance.

Barton Sky has not run for 425 days and returns for John Joseph Hanlon with Harry Sexton claiming — watch his market moves and jumping in the early stages as a flat-footed jumper returning from such a layoff over 3m½f is a serious risk.

Lord Lackendarra's headgear (p) and Dylan Whelan's 7lb claim make him an interesting watch if the pace is strong enough to collapse Le Questionnaire in the final mile, but he needs extreme patience and is fully exposed over this sort of trip on Good ground.

Clone Cross's recent form contains two fallers — watch his jumping in the early stages of this marathon trip, as a departure at a hurdle over 3m½f has far greater consequences than at shorter, and the erratic jumping pattern could affect runners nearby.

races.name: Egan Stone Kilbeggan Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Garnacho
runners_data.note: 7yo prominent racer with two wins and five places from 13 Good-ground starts — excellent going fit — trainer Mark Fahey sends out a 24-day fresh runner with Thomas O'Connor claiming 7lbs, and recent form shows a win followed by a runner-up in identical 2m conditions; well-placed for this shape.

runners_data.name: Linden Arden
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner but has won on Good ground and showed enough at 1/19f to suggest a staying trip is within range; 124-day absence is a flag, T14 return of 1/12 for Kelly gives some encouragement, though racing at the limit of its natural lead role with an amateur claiming 7lbs adds risk at this trip.

runners_data.name: Milan Forth
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has placed twice from five Good-ground runs, handles 2m well but has not won beyond 2m in recent starts; Simon Cavanagh's stable is 0/2 in the last 14 days, and tongue-strap/cheekpieces headgear combination means he needs to dominate early, which will be tougher with Linden Arden in the field.

runners_data.name: Costacurta
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 6yo has been placed in every one of his seven Good-ground starts and is rock-solid in conditions — his 6/7 Good-ground record is the best going-fit in the field; Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride in a yard firing at 6/41 over the last fortnight, making him a serious contender if he tracks efficiently.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: 9yo hold-up horse whose Good-ground record reads 10/15 with a win and three places — a solid match for today's surface — but was pulled up two runs ago and needs to improve on a 4th last time; Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim helps, and the 14-day turnaround for a stable with 0/27 recent returns is a concern for his ability to run to form here.

runners_data.name: Tullybeg
runners_data.note: Veteran 11yo hold-up performer who has run exclusively on Good ground (15/15) and placed three times, suggesting he handles conditions well; Brian McMahon's yard is 1/5 in the past fortnight, and a 60-day absence at this age is not ideal, though the tongue-strap is retained and he stays the trip well having placed at 2m4f and 2m3f.

runners_data.name: Clonbury Bridge
runners_data.note: 10yo prominent runner with two pulls-up in last three starts and a form string of 62P4-P making grim reading; Keith Donoghue takes the ride for a yard with no recent runners in the tracker, and at OR 113 with headgear combinations (tongue-strap, visor) already tried, the question marks around reliability are significant.

runners_data.name: Typical Thomas
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been well beaten in all five recent Good-ground runs, best finish a 4th; Conor Smithers claims 7lbs for James Fahey but the 9yo has not won since distance shown in form and the step up to 2m4½f looks beyond what his finishing kick can deliver in this field.

runners_data.name: Freddie Robdal
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent racer whose best efforts came when dominating smaller fields at 2m, but in a 12-runner field with multiple rivals for the front positions, he is likely to find himself racing off the pace rather than dictating; Dylan Whelan claims 7lbs for De Bromhead, and the tongue-strap is retained, but two DNFs in recent starts and a 17th last time at 2m on Good raise doubts about consistency.

runners_data.name: Prince Palace
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose last five runs have produced three pulled-ups and two 9ths — no placed finish in the period and all recent outings on Soft or Heavy; Mr R Sugrue claims 7lbs but the switch to Good ground from yielding conditions and an OR of 109 with that record makes it very hard to make a case for this runner.

runners_data.name: Grange Walk
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield position by the volume of prominent types in this field — his natural style is patient from the rear, and the redistribution means he is unlikely to get his ideal race; recent form includes a 3rd on Good, trainer Ryan is 6/32 in the last 14 days, and the blinkers are retained, but operating out of role undermines his prospects.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's 6yo is a genuine hold-up type whose natural style is compromised in this shape — like Grange Walk, the hold-up contingent is too large for the race to serve all of them cleanly; two 4ths from 15 Good-ground attempts and a 12-day turnaround suggest he is fit, but no win on Good and no clear route through in midfield makes his task difficult.

races.paceDynamic: Linden Arden is the single confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner handicap chase over 2m4½f on Good ground at Kilbeggan, and with no natural rival to push the pace, Harry Sexton's mount should control proceedings at a comfortable, honest clip rather than a true end-to-end gallop. The field does contain more horses with prominent pretensions than the map can accommodate — Garnacho, Milan Forth, Costacurta, and Clonbury Bridge are all likely to press forward and contest the early positions behind Linden Arden, meaning the race will not be truly slowly run despite just one confirmed leader. Freddie Robdal and Grange Walk are genuine prominent and hold-up horses respectively who are shown in midfield purely because the race shape pushes them out of their natural roles, and their STYLE_FIT flags mean their chance in that compromised position should be discounted. The resulting shape — a controlled lead, a competitive bunch immediately behind, and a clear pace injection before the home turn — strongly favours horses with a prominent or close-tracking style that can travel in the first half and produce their effort from the second-last fence, rather than deep hold-up horses who will find little cover or late injection from this tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Linden Arden sets a measured pace and the prominent trackers behind produce their effort from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: Linden Arden controls the race from the front at a sustainable Good-ground clip, with Garnacho and Costacurta tracking closely enough to pounce inside the final half-mile; the prominent runners who have been racing in their natural role all day are best placed to capitalise as Linden Arden fades under pressure late. This is the dominant shape given one confirmed leader and a cluster of genuine prominent horses directly behind, rewarding those who travel fluently in the first half.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Linden Arden's pace proves sustainable enough and the prominent chasers fail to close the gap from two out.
scenarios.body: Linden Arden, racing from the front in its natural role, sets a rhythm that the big field behind struggles to disrupt cleanly over fences on this undulating track; the 7lb claimer Harry Sexton keeps the horse balanced, and if the pack behind are bunched and unable to quicken in unison, the leader's gap proves decisive. Prominent types who can't accelerate past a relaxed front-runner are the chief losers in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Creep Into Contention
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent bunch overpresses early and tie each other up, leaving genuine late-running horses with a line to thread.
scenarios.body: If Garnacho, Milan Forth, and Costacurta push aggressively for position behind Linden Arden in the early stages and the pace becomes ragged over fences, horses with a natural hold-up or patient style could benefit from a messy final circuit; Rexem and Tullybeg, both genuine hold-up types with strong Good-ground records in this distance range, are the most credible beneficiaries. Note that Grange Walk and Golden Temple, though mapped in midfield, are true hold-up horses and would only feature if they overcome their compromised positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Race, Errors Cost Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or early falls among the prominent bunch strip out the principals and leave a more chaotic contest.
scenarios.body: Kilbeggan's tight, undulating track can punish horses racing prominently at pace over fences, and with a large field of 12 chasing a single front-runner, a miscued jump or two among the prominent cluster could open the race up dramatically inside the final mile. Horses with hold-up profiles who have jumped cleanly in recent starts and covered the trip at this distance would be best placed, but this scenario relies on others' misfortune rather than a structured race shape.

watchPoints.text: Costacurta (De Bromhead/O'Keeffe) has a 6/7 Good-ground placing record and is drawn into the ideal prominent tracking position — if he travels fluently through the first circuit he is the primary danger to the likely pace-setters.

Linden Arden returns from 124 days off and, while confirmed as the front-runner, Harry Sexton's 7lb claim and the long absence mean any sign of laboured jumping in the back straight could unravel the pace scenario entirely.

The cluster of prominent types — Garnacho, Milan Forth, Costacurta, and Clonbury Bridge — racing directly behind a single front-runner over Kilbeggan's tight track creates genuine risk of interference or a jumping error at a critical fence; watch the second and third fences in the back straight where the field bunches.

Rexem (Kenneally 5lb) is the hold-up horse with the best surface record (10/15 on Good) and could creep into the frame if the prominent runners tie each other up — his finishing position in the early stages will indicate whether Scenario C is live.

Grange Walk and Golden Temple are both redistributed true hold-up horses operating out of their natural role; if either is seen racing prominently from the outset, it signals jockey adaptation and could alter the real shape of the race from what the map projects.

races.name: Racing Again On 8th August Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Luimneach
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with course-and-distance form (2nd over 20f on good), trained by Conor O'Dwyer with 1/2 14-day strike, but 54 days off and headgear (ht) add unknowns; sim-going record is modest and finishing at the rear of this large field is a risk.

runners_data.name: Syracus Du Houx
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type, 97 days off the track and trainer McKiernan has a quiet 14-day strike of 0/2; best sim-going figures are unimpressive and the trip is on the sharp side of what he has won at.

runners_data.name: Big Island
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse whose headgear (p) has not transformed his record; Danny Mullins in the plate is an upgrade, but a P-0-F recent form string and a 41-day absence make confidence difficult in a race where his natural position at the rear is already congested.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Honey
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer with the best sim-going strike rate in the field (12/15 on good), placed twice over 21f on good including a second in similar company; the headgear (b) is retained and only 20 days since last run keeps him sharp — well placed to sit behind Mercurial Sea and challenge.

runners_data.name: Doyen Magic
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has produced two placed efforts in recent form (2-2), and trainer Rothwell has a strong 14-day record of 2/22; however, the sim-going figures are modest and the step back to good ground from heavy/soft outings deserves a note.

runners_data.name: Island McCoo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins and two places from nine good-ground runs, won over 24f on good at OR 88 just 14 days ago; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim sweetens the weight and the headgear (t) is retained — a live candidate to press the pace throughout.

runners_data.name: My Policy
runners_data.note: Sits in a prominent role and has a remarkable sim-going record of 12/13 appearances on good ground, albeit without a win; the headgear (p) is kept and the recent placed effort over 18f on good gives encouragement, though the jump to 20f is yet to be proven in a winning context.

runners_data.name: Watty Show
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse, displaced to midfield on this map due to sheer field size — a fading tendency is flagged in his profile, and his sim-going record on good shows 0 wins from 6 competitive runs; De Bromhead sends him here fresh enough at 41 days but the compromised position makes his chance harder to construct.

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: An out-and-out hold-up type at 10 years old who has been placed into midfield on this map by overcrowding at the rear; the 7-day turnaround from Ryan's yard is notable, but his recent form string of P-9-6-8-7 on good ground gives little encouragement regardless of where he ends up in the field.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran second over 24f on good and has four placed efforts from good-ground starts under Gavin Cromwell; headgear (t) retained and the 21-day freshener suits — a capable hold-up/prominent type who could creep into frame calculations if the race develops late.

runners_data.name: Ixigreczed
runners_data.note: Carries a fading-in-finish flag and a finish-fading headgear (b) note; genuine hold-up profile pushed to midfield on this map, and a form string of 0-6-0-0-5 on good ground (sim-going: 11/15) reflects consistent underperformance — the style mismatch is compounded by the form.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up type entered just 7 days after his last run, both from John Patrick Ryan's yard; placed on good ground four times in the last five (sim-going 9/15) but the redistribution from his natural rear position undermines the profile, and P-P recent form adds concern.

runners_data.name: Battle Of Benburb
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with excellent good-ground sim-going (12/15) and a win and three places in that sample, but 109 days off the track is a major flag; form string of PP-7-PP suggests the engine may not be firing — needs to bounce out sharp after the break.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with a positive form string of 0-5-3-1-4-3 and a win over 24f on good ground from John Patrick Ryan's yard (third runner from that stable today, 7-day turnaround); the most believable late threat if the pace collapse enables a midfield horse to close, given a genuine placed record at this trip on this going.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Hanlon (0/23 14-day strike is notable) with a 7-day turnaround; headgear (p) is in place and he has placed once in five good-ground runs, but a form string of 0-F-9-0-5 and the congested hold-up position make a winning chance hard to see.

runners_data.name: Walkmethroughit
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with a fading-in-finish flag, mapped to midfield due to overcrowding; the 134-day layoff is a major concern and sim-going on good is sparse (2/7), making him a risk both fitness-wise and tactically in a race where his preferred rear position is simply unavailable.

runners_data.name: Mercurial Sea
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, which gives him uncontested control of the pace; the style-fit tag (0.93) reflects that he is coded prominent but acts as a genuine lead horse here — five good-ground starts have produced four placed efforts and the 10-day freshener is a positive for a young five-year-old.

races.paceDynamic: Mercurial Sea is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine pace-maker to challenge for the lead, should stride out alone and dictate a sustainable gallop over the 2m4½f trip on good ground at Kilbeggan. With no rival likely to hunt him down from the off, the tempo will be controlled and even rather than frenetic, meaning the race will be set up as a stamina test that unfolds from the front rather than a sprint finish off a crawl. Hurricane Honey and Island McCoo are the principal prominent types who can tuck in behind Mercurial Sea and hunt the leaders, making them the most dangerous challengers in this shape. The race shape strongly favours prominent/front-end racers who can travel smoothly in the first three or four and pounce before the hold-up brigade can unleash their finish — this field contains far more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Watty Show, Walkmethroughit, Ferdia, Kilashee, and Ixigreczed all redistributed to midfield and unlikely to find their natural ground-saving position, which further tilts the advantage toward those who race prominently.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mercurial Sea Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mercurial Sea dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mercurial Sea sets a sustainable pace solo, giving himself every chance to find the extra on the run-in as rivals burn energy trying to make up ground from midfield and the rear; the good ground and manageable trip suit a front-runner with proven placed form at the distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Hurricane Honey or Island McCoo track Mercurial Sea through the race and overhaul him in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two prominent types closest to the pace have proven course/distance form and go well on good ground, giving them the platform to travel economically and challenge when Mercurial Sea's advantage shrinks at the final fences; this shape rewards horses who race without cover and switch off cleanly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Mercurial Sea's lead is greater than expected, allowing the front-runners to tire, with midfield horses arriving with a late run.
scenarios.body: Love Like This has genuine positive form figures at similar distances on good ground and is a natural beneficiary if the pace-setter stops quickly in the straight; My Cullen and Luimneach could also reach the frame if the ground and distance bring stamina to the fore.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the redistributed hold-up types manage to secure a better position than expected, getting a clear run to the line.
scenarios.body: This is materially less likely because Watty Show, Ferdia, Kilashee, Walkmethroughit, and Ixigreczed are all racing out of their natural role having been pushed forward by overcrowding at the rear, and finishing fades are flagged against several of them; without true cover and a strong gallop to aim at, their hold-up profiles are compromised.

watchPoints.text: Mercurial Sea goes out alone in front — watch whether any of the prominent horses (Hurricane Honey, Island McCoo) can close the gap from the second fence, as his ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest shape-defining factor in this race.

Love Like This is the third runner in 7 days from John Patrick Ryan's yard alongside Ferdia and Kilashee — watch for signs of a yard in form and whether any of the three gets a race-fit bounce in the straight.

Walkmethroughit returns from 134 days off on going that is much better than his form figures suggest he handles (sim-going only 2/7 on comparable surfaces) — watch for early signs of greenness or laboured jumping that could affect those around him in a 17-runner field.

Battle Of Benburb has a strong good-ground profile (12/15 sim-going, 1W3P) but returns after 109 days absent — watch whether he jumps out with intent from the front, as a freshened prominent type could exploit the single-pace setter scenario if Mercurial Sea shows any sign of vulnerability.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Watty Show, Ferdia, Kilashee, Ixigreczed, Walkmethroughit) all forced into midfield creates a congestion risk at the early fences in a 17-runner chase — watch the first two fences carefully for interference that could unsettle the genuine prominent horses tracking Mercurial Sea.
